chunk_findings.detail: When `it.base_sha` is missing, `fork = it.base_sha or landed_before` makes both probes the same revision: `moved = changed_paths(landed_before, tip=landed_before)` is an empty successful diff, so `files = mine ∩ moved` is empty and no `merge.reconciled` is appended. Given an item with no `base_sha` whose branch and another item both changed `src/foo.py` since the real fork, complete is not held. That is fail-open, unlike the `changed_paths is None` branches in the same function, which record a reconcile on purpose.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/merge.py:_record_reconciled

It never checks the gate against `reconciled["main"]` or that the run names `reconciled["files"]`. Given `reconciled = {files: ["src/foo.py"], main: "bbb", at: "2026-10-17T12:00:00Z"}` and a `unit_tests` PASS at `2026-10-17T12:00:01Z` recorded on the pre-merge branch (commit `ccc`, foo tests not re-run on `bbb`), the function returns `""` and complete is allowed. That is the fail-open case the guard is supposed to close: a later stamp is not the reconciled tree.

chunk_findings.detail: `names_reconciled_tree` returns True if any reconciled path is a substring of `evidence["note"]`, and never consults `tree_sha` in that branch. A post-reconcile `unit_tests` PASS whose note merely mentions the path therefore counts as proof the suite ran on the reconciled tree, even when `tree_sha` names a different commit. Given `reconciled = {files: ["src/x.py"], main: "b"*40}` and a gate recorded at/after `reconciled["at"]` with `evidence = {note: "pre-merge suite, touched src/x.py", tree_sha: "c"*40}`, the filename check succeeds, `passed_on_reconciled_tree("unit_tests")` is True, and complete is not refused. The added test only uses a note that omits the path, so it does not catch this.

chunk_findings.detail: `names_reconciled_tree` treats a run as on the reconciled commit when the 12-character `reconciled["main"]` prefix is any substring of `evidence["tree_sha"]`, not a prefix of that sha. Given `reconciled["main"]` starting `1234567890ab` and a post-`at` `unit_tests` PASS whose `tree_sha` is `deadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeef1234567890ab` (a different commit whose hash merely contains those 12 characters, or a note-like blob `"built 1234567890ab then tested tree fff…"`), the function returns True and `_reconciled_blocker` returns `""`, so complete is allowed without a suite on the reconciled tree. The check should be a prefix match (`startswith` / the recorded sha starting with `tree_sha`), which is what the comment claims and what the fail-closed tree proof requires.

chunk_findings.detail: When a post-reconcile PASS has no `tree_sha`, `names_reconciled_tree` treats any note that merely contains a reconciled path as proof the run was on the reconciled commit (`f in note`). Given `reconciled["files"] == ["flow.py"]` (or `src/util.py`) and a `unit_tests` PASS at or after `at` whose evidence is only `{"note": "overflow.py still green"}` (or `"touched src/util.py.bak"`), `"flow.py" in "overflow.py still green"` is True, so the function returns True, `_reconciled_blocker` returns `""`, and complete is allowed without a run on `reconciled["main"]`. The same hole fires for any shorter path that is a substring of a longer name in the note.
